name: soc2-pi1
title: SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria — Processing Integrity (PI1.3-PI1.5) slice
description: Vectors evidencing the narrow, genuine SOC 2 fit CIS-2 has: complete/accurate records of input, processing, and output activity (PI1.3-PI1.5), plus a partial fit to CC7.1/CC7.3 anomaly detection. See compliance/CROSSWALK.md rows 10-19 and its 'SOC 2 honest verdict' for the full picture, including everything this profile does NOT touch (governance, vendor mgmt, vuln scanning, confidentiality, availability).

vectors.crosswalk_control: CROSSWALK.md row 16 (PI1.3 records of system inputs)
vectors.rationale: The receipt's prompt field + digest is the recorded input activity PI1.3 asks for.

vectors.crosswalk_control: CROSSWALK.md row 17 (PI1.4 records of processing activity)
vectors.rationale: The hash chain is the 'recorded completely and accurately' guarantee for processing activity across the whole log, not just one record.

vectors.crosswalk_control: CROSSWALK.md row 18 (PI1.5 records of system output activity)
vectors.rationale: Confirms the output record (logged token ids) is complete and matches what was actually emitted -- 'complete and accurate' per PI1.5's own language.

vectors.crosswalk_control: CROSSWALK.md row 13 (CC7.3 detection tools identifying anomalies) and row 17 (PI1.4 error detection half)
vectors.rationale: A digest-mismatch-on-tamper / replay-on-duplicate detection is exactly the 'detection tool... to identify anomalies' language of CC7.3, for the compute slice only.

vectors.crosswalk_control: CROSSWALK.md row 16-18 (PI1.3-PI1.5) — records must bind to the real system component that ran
vectors.rationale: NOT COVERED by the v0.1 scaffold today -- see vector detail. A record that doesn't bind to the actual model instance is not a trustworthy PI1 input/processing/output record.

vectors.crosswalk_control: CROSSWALK.md row 16 (PI1.3) — the input record must bind to the actual input
vectors.rationale: NOT COVERED by the v0.1 scaffold today -- see vector detail.

not_covered: CC1-CC6, CC8, CC9 (governance, access control, change management, risk assessment, vendor management) — organizational, not a product feature CIS-2 ships.
CC7.2 (vulnerability scanning) — CIS-2 is not a vulnerability scanner.
A1.1/A1.2 beyond the backup-artifact sliver — availability posture of the whole system.
C1.1/C1.2 (confidentiality) — receipts may themselves contain sensitive prompt/output content requiring a separate access-control policy this suite does not provide or check.
'Correction' half of PI1.4 (errors are detected AND corrected) — CIS-2 detects; correction is a procedural/ops action outside this suite.

A real SOC 2 Type II report — requires an independent licensed CPA-firm auditor and a 6-12 month operating-effectiveness observation period across ALL criteria the company puts in scope, not just PI1.
